audience: Small and medium business owners anywhere in India, in any industry (anyone who talks to customers), plus freelancers and agencies for the lead-gen service. Work is done fully online, in English and Hindi/Hinglish.

facts_rules: No testimonials, client names, results, or statistics exist yet. Never invent any.
Only quote prices that appear in price_note. Never promise rankings, revenue or guaranteed results.
Primary goal of every post: earn DMs/messages.
Audience is all of India: do not assume one city or state; use examples from varied industries and cities, and national (not city-specific) hashtags.
Any project shown is a sample, demo or concept project unless stated otherwise by the owner; never describe it as client work.
Posts must read as a developer showing real work, not as an advertisement.
Do not state counts or timeframes about the owner's work (projects built, days taken, clients) unless given here.

NO DEMO CLAIMS. Never say or imply that the owner built, configured, set up or prepared a demo, sample, prototype or custom example for any business or business type ('I built a chatbot for homestays', 'I configured a sample', 'test it yourself', 'live demo link'). Never offer a demo, demo link, sample, mock-up or personalised example. You may explain in general how a chatbot, ad or lead sheet works, and may use an illustrative example conversation clearly labelled as an example.
NO FABRICATED WORK. Do not claim any specific piece of work exists unless it is listed in this file.

Write for ANY small business in India. Never target a single niche (hotels, homestays, cafes, clinics, gyms...). The scenario and the message must be relatable to every business that talks to customers; at most mention 2-3 example business types in one line.

LEAD GEN AUDIENCE: lead-gen posts speak to EVERY freelancer, agency or solo service seller who needs clients from local businesses, whatever they sell. Never address one profession: do not call the reader a web developer, developer, coder or website designer, and do not make 'businesses with no website' the main example (that only helps web developers). Open with 'Freelancers', 'Agencies' or 'Anyone selling a service', not with a skill. Describe the sheet only in general terms: local businesses found through Google Places with contact details, review counts and website checks, including newly opened ones. Do not invent other signals or columns. Use only broad hashtags (#FreelanceIndia #Freelancers #LeadGeneration #GetClients #SmallBusinessIndia), never profession tags such as #WebDeveloper, #WebDesign or #AgencyLife.

Only offers allowed in posts: (1) 'pay after approval' on every service (the client pays only after approving the work); (2) a short conversation: the reader DMs and the owner replies with honest advice on whether the service fits their business. A free quick look at a website with 3 things to fix is allowed ONLY in website posts. Nothing else free: no demos, samples, audits, discounts, guarantees or refunds.

NO ABSOLUTE OUTCOME CLAIMS. Never say a service eliminates, ends, kills, removes or guarantees a problem or result ('friction khatam', 'without the drop-off', 'kill your leads', 'you will never lose a lead'). Use soft, honest wording: 'can reduce', 'helps', 'makes it easier'.

languages.instagram: Hindi written in Hinglish (Roman script), everyday spoken Hindi with English tech words

offers.pay_after_approval: Applies to every service: the client pays only after approving the work.

schedule.note: Websites are saturated in India: 1 post per week only. Core = priority 1 (chatbots, AI ads, lead gen), rotating by least recently used. Weekdays: Monday=0. One reel a day on Instagram, posted manually.

instagram.note: Weekday numbers: Monday=0 ... Sunday=6. On these days you post the reel yourself (the draft includes the 3 Flow prompts). On every other day the approved image + caption is posted to Instagram automatically.
